Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, both required skill guides, and the current rollout artifacts. I’ll use the wake-visual skill to inspect both 3D views before editing, then use the fish-control shelf’s structured transfer protocol for the single candidate and document any transferred invariant explicitly.

The contract confirms this is a single-file policy edit, with provenance and durable guidance both mandatory. I’m now anchoring the visual review to every sampled score/termination and inherited optimizer note; no architecture choice will be made until that comparison is complete.

Both visual rows agree on the key distinction: all samples self-propel with a coherent alternating wake, but the posterior-only prefill carries larger 3D vortex structures/load exposure and stays in the upper corridor, while the `0.828L` near-miss preserves a compact wake long enough to cross the target neighborhood before departing left. I’m cross-checking that apparent pass-by against trajectory, joint/limit, force, and control-state data before selecting a near-target mechanism.

The assigned parent contains three consecutive completed descendants with essentially the same near-miss and termination (`0.8278L`, `0.8318L`, `0.8306L`, all left-domain), so the shelf’s re-consultation trigger is met. I’m applying it now at the mechanism level—looking for a normalized near-target interception invariant, not another gain-only retune.

The inherited artifacts include more than scalar scores: full step-11/12 notes, policies, trajectories, and both visual sheets are present under the sampled guidance logs. I found that the anterior same-side reflex and the anterior counter-sweep both preserved the pass-by, with only millimetric closest-approach changes; I’m reading those exact implementations and images now so this candidate does not repeat either mechanism.

The repeated terminal policies are visually and dynamically indistinguishable because they all retain a settled same-sign C-bend while the body yaws but the velocity vector does not follow. The new hypothesis is a state-selected gait transition: on an inbound unsafe intercept, once the C-bend is attained, smoothly release the static redirect into the already-evidenced phase-separated traveling carrier so the two joints execute a full dynamic course-correction stroke. This is distinct from deeper curvature, a one-joint pulse/counter-sweep, and the weak neutral-anterior/posterior recoil.

The policy, provenance note, and durable lesson are now updated. The far-field law is the evaluated near-miss parent; only the inbound, unsafe, attained-bend regime can switch from the static redirect into the full traveling carrier. I’m validating that locality, activation, symmetry, boundedness, and parameter ownership hold on frozen rollout states before invoking the required independent checker.

Frozen replay showed the first gate was too late: requiring both joints to settle activated only from `0.863L` inward, leaving almost no time to rotate velocity. I’m tightening the mechanism—not its gain—so observed anterior C-bend attainment starts the full two-joint carrier stroke; that preserves the state-selected C-start invariant while giving the evidenced course deficit time to respond.

Local guidance, Julia contract, and edit-boundary checks pass. I’m now invoking the workspace-required independent check-runner from `.codex/agents/check-runner.toml`; it will rerun the three prescribed non-CFD checks and report only contract validity.

The configured checker role could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this account. The checks themselves already pass locally; I’m retrying the same immutable `.toml` procedure with an independent default agent so the required second-pass validation is still completed without CFD.

The independent fallback checker reports PASS on all three prescribed checks: material guidance/notes, Julia policy contract (including schema/finite action), and solver edit boundary. No CFD was run. I’m doing the final artifact/nonempty and whitespace review, then I’ll hand off the candidate for EvE evaluation.

Implemented exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) — terminal dynamic-carrier recovery triggered by unsafe intercept, closing motion, and anterior bend attainment.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) — visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer block, falsification criteria, and frozen-state audit.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:89) — materially revised reusable lesson covering the failed terminal branches.

All three prescribed non-CFD checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract/schema, and editable-boundary validation. Frozen replay confirms zero changes beyond `1.75L`, reflection equivariance, and bounded finite actions. Formal CFD was not run.
